scope: Exact public saved packets and real passing decisions; replay is a host/prompt/schema contract regression, not a new inference-quality test.

issues.title: Missing IDs crash update and destroy
issues.reason: `where(...).first` returns `nil` when the requested host does not exist. `update` passes that value to `save_host`, which immediately calls `host.host=`, while `destroy` calls `host.destroy`; both paths therefore raise `NoMethodError` and return a 500 for stale, deleted, or invalid IDs instead of a controlled not-found response. This is reachable through ordinary CRUD requests and also creates noisy server exceptions.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Look up the record with the application's standard not-found mechanism (for example `find(params[:id])` if `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` is centrally rendered as 404), or explicitly render a 404 before calling `save_host`/`destroy` when the lookup returns nil.

issues.title: Configured ports never match referers
issues.reason: `ensure_embeddable` now relies exclusively on `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`. Exact proposed-tree source in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:1-18` shows that the model validation explicitly accepts stored values such as `example.com:3000`, while `record_for_host` parses the referer and compares only `uri.host` (which is `example.com`, without the port) against the stored `host`. Consequently, every embed request for a valid configured host-with-port is rejected with `InvalidAccess`, so development/staging deployments and any non-default-port installation cannot use this supported configuration.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make the lookup preserve an explicitly configured referer port (for example, compare against `uri.host` plus `:port` for non-default ports), while retaining the current hostname-only match for entries without a port. Add a model/controller test for an allowed host configured with a port.

issues.title: Canonicalize both sides of host lookup
issues.reason: `URI#host` excludes the port, while the validation permits a port and the callback preserves it. Therefore a valid saved value such as `example.com:3000` can never match `record_for_host('http://example.com:3000')`. The comparison also lowercases only the database column; an uppercase hostname returned from the input URI is compared as-is and can fail against the lowercased column. These cases reject explicitly valid configured hosts.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Store and compare one canonical representation. For example, normalize saved values to the parsed lowercase hostname (and deliberately decide whether ports are part of authorization); if ports are retained, compare both `uri.host` and `uri.port`. At minimum lowercase the lookup value before comparing.

issues.title: Handle blank host before normalization
issues.reason: The admin controller assigns the request value directly and calls `save`. If `host` is missing or null, this callback invokes `sub!` on `nil` before the format validator can add an error, turning invalid input into a server error instead of the controller's normal validation response.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Guard normalization when `host` is blank (or normalize with a nil-safe operation), and add a presence validation so blank input reaches `render_json_error` rather than raising.

issues.title: Configured hosts with ports are rejected
issues.reason: `EmbeddableHost` explicitly accepts and retains values such as `example.com:3000`, but `record_for_host` extracts only `URI#host` before querying (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:15`), yielding `example.com`. Consequently this changed authorization call treats a URL like `https://example.com:3000/article` as invalid even when `example.com:3000` is configured, so retrieval never runs for valid port-specific embed sources.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compare the configured host against a normalized authority that includes the explicit port when present, and add a model or retriever test covering an allowed non-default port.

issues.title: Restrict routes to implemented actions
issues.reason: An unconstrained `resources` declaration creates all seven REST routes, including `index`, `show`, `new`, and `edit`. The exact proposed controller source (`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, lines 1–35) implements only `create`, `update`, and `destroy`. Requests to the other newly registered admin routes therefore dispatch to nonexistent actions instead of being absent from the API, producing `ActionNotFound` responses and potentially surfacing as server errors.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Declare only the controller's implemented actions: `resources :embeddable_hosts, only: [:create, :update, :destroy], constraints: AdminConstraint.new`.

issues.title: Missing category row crashes migration
issues.reason: The query can legitimately return zero rows when `embed_category` has no persisted override or names a category that no longer exists. Indexing `[0]['id']` then raises before the `category_id == 0` fallback runs, aborting the database migration and therefore deployment. The proposed settings configuration also no longer defines `embed_category`, while `uncategorized_category_id` remains the available fallback (`config/site_settings.yml`, embedding and category-ID sections).
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Read the first result defensively and use the uncategorized category ID when no matching row exists. The fallback query should likewise handle a missing row explicitly rather than dereferencing it blindly.

issues.title: Migration cannot be rolled back
issues.reason: This `change` migration contains raw `execute` calls for inserts and deletes. Active Record cannot automatically reverse those commands, so rolling back this migration raises an irreversible-migration error instead of removing the new table and restoring the migrated settings. The final deletion also destroys the original setting rows, making a correct rollback require explicit reconstruction.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Replace `change` with explicit `up` and `down` methods. In `down`, reconstruct the legacy settings from `embeddable_hosts` before dropping the table, including an explicit policy for hosts assigned to different categories.

issues.title: Save can apply the wrong category
issues.reason: `props.category_id` is captured before the asynchronous save, but the success callback reads the mutable `categoryId` again. The category chooser remains enabled while `host.isSaving`, so a user can select category A, save, and then select category B before the request completes. The server stores A, while the component assigns and displays B. A later edit can consequently overwrite the persisted category based on this incorrect client state.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Capture `categoryId` once at the beginning of `save()` and use that same value for both the request and the success callback. Alternatively, disable the category chooser while saving.

issues.title: Cancelled hosts remain in the store
issues.reason: `addHost` creates an Ember Data record, while cancelling a new host invokes this action. Removing it only from `embeddable_hosts` does not unload or delete the new record, leaving a dirty unsaved record registered in the store. Repeated add/cancel operations therefore accumulate orphaned records and can affect later store-level record access.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: When removing a new host, also unload or delete the record using the Ember Data API supported by this project. Keep the existing collection removal for persisted hosts after successful deletion.

issues.title: Icon buttons lack accessible names
issues.reason: The save, cancel, edit, and delete buttons provide only icons and no `label` or `title`. Unlike other icon-only `d-button` usages that supply a translated title, these controls expose no textual description, so screen-reader users cannot determine their actions.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Add localized `title` or `label` values describing each button's action (save, cancel, edit, and delete).

issues.title: Controller actions have no behavioral coverage
issues.reason: This sole example only verifies the superclass. The proposed controller has authorization filters plus `create`, `update`, `destroy`, and save-error behavior (exact proposed-tree source at `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3-31`), but this spec sends no requests and asserts none of their responses or side effects. Consequently, regressions in permissions, persistence, validation errors, default category assignment, or missing-record handling can pass this suite unchanged.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Replace or supplement the inheritance assertion with focused request examples for non-staff access and for create/update/destroy success and failure paths, including invalid attributes and unknown IDs.

issues.title: Controller behavior remains untested
issues.reason: This assertion only checks Ruby inheritance. It never sends a request, so the controller's staff-access filters and serialized response contract can regress while this spec continues to pass. Add request examples covering unauthorized access and the successful `show` response, including its `embedding` root and host data.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Replace or supplement the inheritance assertion with request-level examples for a non-staff user and a staff user, asserting the access result and serialized response shape.

issues.title: Missing hosts cause server errors
issues.reason: Both `update` and `destroy` use `.first`, which returns `nil` for an unknown ID. `update` then passes `nil` to `save_host`, where `host.host=` raises `NoMethodError`; `destroy` similarly calls `destroy` on `nil`. Thus authenticated admin requests for stale or nonexistent records return a 500 rather than a controlled 404 response.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Load the host with `find(params[:id])` so the framework's normal record-not-found handling returns a 404, or explicitly render a not-found response when `.first` returns `nil`. Apply the same handling to both update and destroy.

issues.title: Missing category crashes migration
issues.reason: The query can return zero rows when `embed_category` is absent or its value no longer matches a category name. Indexing `[0]['id']` then calls `[]` on `nil`, aborting the migration before the intended `category_id == 0` fallback runs. The fallback query at line 14 has the same unchecked-row problem, so a missing `uncategorized_category_id` setting also crashes deployment.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Read each query row defensively and fall back when it is absent. If neither category lookup produces an ID, raise a clear migration error before creating or deleting migrated data.

issues.title: Migration cannot restore deleted settings
issues.reason: The migration is declared with `change` but executes raw SQL and permanently deletes the source settings. Rails cannot automatically reverse these `execute` calls, and even a table drop would not recreate the deleted `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` values. Rolling back this deployment therefore either raises an irreversible-migration error or leaves the previous application version without its configuration.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Replace `change` with explicit `up` and `down` methods. In `down`, reconstruct and restore both legacy settings from the new table/category records before dropping `embeddable_hosts`, or explicitly preserve the original setting values so rollback is lossless.
issues.codeSnippet: execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"

issues.title: Migrated URL-form hosts no longer pass authorization
issues.reason:
The migration inserts each legacy setting value directly into the new table, bypassing `EmbeddableHost` normalization. Legacy configuration explicitly supported entries such as `http://eviltrout.com`, but `record_for_host` now extracts `eviltrout.com` and compares it directly with the stored value. A migrated row containing the scheme therefore never matches.
Evidence: PRF024 migrates raw newline-separated setting entries through SQL rather than model callbacks. PRF011 only strips schemes and paths in a `before_validation` callback, which the SQL insert bypasses, and its lookup compares parsed `URI#host` directly with the database column. PRF033 and PRF038 make that lookup authoritative for embed access and retrieval. PRF044 demonstrates that URL-form legacy entries were supported before migration.
Business impact: After deployment, previously authorized embedding sites configured with schemes or paths stop loading comments and importing embedded topics until every affected row is manually rewritten.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Normalize each legacy entry before insertion using the same canonical form as `EmbeddableHost`—at minimum remove the scheme and path and normalize case—or migrate through a migration-local model that runs equivalent validation and normalization. Add an upgrade test covering legacy `http://`, `https://`, and path-form entries.

issues.title: Refresh response shape causes token refresh failure
issues.reason: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the native `fetch` `Response` object directly (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:6-14`). This caller still accesses `tokenInfo.data.error` and later `tokenInfo.data.access_token`, but a `Response` has no `data` property. Expired Bigin credentials therefore throw while checking `tokenInfo.data.error` instead of refreshing successfully.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Normalize the shared helper's result to the Axios-like `{ data }` shape expected here, or update this caller to parse the fetch response with `await tokenInfo.json()` before reading the token payload.

issues.title: One refresh caller sends a credential ID as a user ID
issues.reason:
One refresh caller sends a credential ID as a user ID
`refreshOAuthTokens` treats its third argument as the Cal.com `userId` and sends it as `calcomUserId`. Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId`, unlike the other updated callers that pass `credential.userId`.
Evidence: The helper parameter is named `userId` and serializes it as `calcomUserId` (`PRF002`). Bigin supplies `credentialId` (`PRF040`), while Office 365 video supplies `credential.userId` (`PRF006`), demonstrating inconsistent identifier routing.
Business impact: Credential synchronization can be applied to the wrong account or fail during Bigin token refresh, creating authentication outages and cross-account credential corruption risk.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Pass the owning `userId` to the shared helper, or change the sync contract to explicitly accept and resolve a credential ID. Use distinct parameter names and types so the two identifiers cannot be mixed.

issues.title: Sequence parsing can cross declared boundary
issues.reason: The loop only stops when `length <= 0`; it never rejects a child whose encoded size exceeds the sequence's declared content length. For example, a sequence declaring length 2 can contain a 3-byte child, causing the decoder to consume bytes outside the sequence and still return successfully. Malformed ASN.1 can therefore be accepted as a valid sequence and subsequent parsing can operate on data beyond the declared container.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Reject any child whose encoded length exceeds the remaining sequence length, and require the remaining length to reach exactly zero before returning.

issues.title: Indefinite-length sequences are silently accepted
issues.reason: When `readLength()` returns `-1` for an indefinite-length encoding, `while (length > 0)` is skipped and `readSequence()` returns an empty sequence without consuming or validating the end-of-contents marker. This accepts a non-DER encoding as an apparently valid empty sequence and can leave trailing sequence data to be interpreted outside its container.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Reject indefinite-length encodings in this DER decoder, or explicitly parse and validate the end-of-contents marker and nested content boundaries.

issues.title: Malformed DER can be accepted by the ECDSA signature conversion path
issues.reason:
Malformed DER can be accepted by the ECDSA signature conversion path
The DER decoder is directly used by `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` to parse ECDSA signatures, but `readSequence()` does not enforce that each child stays within the declared sequence length and also returns successfully for indefinite-length sequences. Consequently, malformed or non-DER signature encodings can be converted into concatenated `r||s` values instead of being rejected at the crypto boundary.
Evidence: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS()` calls `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()` and then parses the returned integers, while `readSequence()` subtracts child lengths without rejecting an overrun and skips validation when `readLength()` returns `-1`. The test suite covers only valid round trips.
Business impact: Malformed ECDSA signatures may be accepted by the conversion layer, weakening input validation and potentially causing inconsistent verification behavior across providers.
issues.suggestedFixDescription: Make the decoder strict DER: reject indefinite lengths, enforce child boundaries against the declared sequence length, require the remaining length to reach exactly zero, and add malformed-input tests through `asn1derToConcatenatedRS()`.

covered_summaries.rationale: Finding 2 is a bundled cross-file summary of two distinct decoder defects fully covered by findings 0 and 1: child-length overrun beyond a sequence boundary, and acceptance of indefinite-length encodings. Findings 0 and 1 state the respective triggers, malformed-input acceptance, parsing impacts, and corrective changes. Finding 2 adds caller-path context and test guidance but no separate causal defect.

Finding 2 bundles exactly the two distinct decoder root causes retained separately by findings 0 and 1: child encodings overrunning the declared sequence boundary, and indefinite-length encodings bypassing sequence parsing and validation. Together, findings 0 and 1 preserve the malformed-input triggers, acceptance and trailing-data impacts, and required strict-DER corrections. Finding 2's ECDSA conversion-path details and malformed-input test recommendation are cross-file impact evidence and validation guidance for those same defects, not an additional causal defect.
